capabilities: Novel mechanism — the claim pack is transferable on resale because it is bound to the product serial + sealed purchase proof (buyer mandate ref + retailer receipt ref), not to a retailer account login. verify_pack recomputes the seal from the serial, bindings, and transfer chain alone — no account credential, no original-holder proof. Bench: register → transfer in one process, then verify_pack by pack_id only in a fresh process = VALID with the original holder uninvolved; the exported pack object also verifies VALID in the fresh process with bindings intact.

Sealed bindings + chained transfers: the five bindings (serial, product_ref, buyer_mandate_ref, retailer_receipt_ref, purchase_ts) are immutable at registration; transfer appends a chained record (each transfer's prev_seal equals the actual superseded seal, genesis prev_hash GENESIS) and re-seals without ever editing the bindings. Bench tamper matrix: 5/5 bound fields → INVALID, 11/11 chain tampers → INVALID, 6/6 supplied-pack attacks (seal transplant, naive SHA-256 reseal without the HMAC key, chain truncation + holder rollback, replayed duplicate transfer, seal deleted, mandate swap) → INVALID; a tampered pack refuses transfer with PACK_INVALID and claim_check reports transferable:false.

Full-content seal (v0.1.1 fix for bench defect D1, MEDIUM): the seal now covers the complete pack object minus the seal field, and verify enforces strict structure — any key outside the specced top-level/binding/transfer sets, a missing or wrong-typed field, or a scope/seal_type outside the spec vocabulary (scope must be exactly LOCAL/fixture) verifies INVALID, supplied or stored. get_pack refuses structurally out-of-spec stored packs (PACK_INVALID) instead of serving injected or relabelled content as sealed pack content. Re-bench D1 attacks PASS 26/26, including bindings.injected_coverage = 'lifetime-full' and a top-level scope relabel to 'LIVE/production' — both INVALID.

Advertised schemas enforced at dispatch (v0.1.1 fix for bench defect D2, LOW): required fields present, declared types exact (an int purchase_ts or a list serial is a clean validation error, never coerced via str()), and extra argument keys rejected per additionalProperties: false. capabilities: Novel mechanism — session-bound fingerprint chain: pin_session canonical-hashes (toolprint-canonical-v1, SPEC §3) every tool's name + description + inputSchema at session start and stores the pin as the genesis of a hash-chained session record; verify_call recomputes the hash of the exact description/schema presented at call time — presented hash == pinned hash = VALID, any difference = INVALIDATED, appended to the chain as a proof record carrying BOTH hashes. A swapped description cannot be quietly un-swapped: swap-back returns VALID again but the INVALIDATED proof record stays in the chain, unaltered. Bench: independent canonicalizer (written from SPEC §3 alone) reproduces all fixture fingerprints + the session fingerprint byte-exact; a 1-character description edit and a schema-only property change both INVALIDATE; bundled swaps give drift CHANGED×2 / SAME×1 / ADDED×0 / REMOVED×0 exactly; list reorder does NOT invalidate (fingerprints are per-tool, session tools sorted by name).

Session-bound, not a static scan: a tool list fully clean at pin time whose description is swapped AFTER pinning is caught by verify_call — a static pre-flight scanner (e.g. mcp-scan) has no session state to catch a post-pin swap. Controls bench-verified: verify on an unpinned session = UNKNOWN_SESSION (never VALID), on a never-pinned tool = UNKNOWN_TOOL, with a never-pinned description = INVALIDATED; unknown tool names (e.g. proxy_call) = NO_SUCH_TOOL refusal stating it does not proxy live MCP traffic.

Caller-anchored chain head (v0.1.1 fix for bench defect D1, MEDIUM): a bare hash chain is internally consistent after its LAST record is deleted, so tail truncation — typically deleting the INVALIDATED proof record — was undetectable in v0.1. v0.1.1 returns head_hash + record_count from pin_session, verify_call, and get_session_chain, and get_session_chain accepts them back as expected_head_hash / expected_record_count: anchored tail truncation = chain_valid:false, TAIL_TRUNCATION_SUSPECTED; a same-count forged tail = CHAIN_HEAD_MISMATCH; interior tamper (edit / delete / reorder of any non-tail record) stays self-detecting with no anchor needed (CHAIN_RECOMPUTE_FAILED). Without an anchor the response carries anchored:false and chain_valid asserts internal consistency only — never implied truncation detection (SPEC §10; caller duty: anchor at pin, re-anchor after every verify).

Independent recompute by design: fingerprint_tool returns the exact canonical JSON preimage of every fingerprint, so any caller can recompute every hash with any SHA-256 implementation; detect_drift reports per-tool SAME / CHANGED / ADDED / REMOVED vs the pin with both fingerprints, read-only (drift checks never append to the chain). Ledger-membership verification + terms-seal enforcement (v0.1.1 fixes for bench defects D1/D2): VALID is returned only for a receipt present in the sealed ledger passing the full per-publisher chain walk — a standalone object resealed with the public formula (forged crawler, fingerprint of content never crawled, or an identity swap of a genuine receipt) verifies INVALID with chain_valid: false (re-bench C1: 10/10). record_crawl and verify_receipt recompute the terms-record seal before trusting stored terms: a seal-broken terms record refuses minting (TERMS_SEAL_INVALID) and drives prior receipts INVALID with terms_status: seal_invalid, per-record (re-bench C2: 12/12).

capabilities: Novel mechanism — probe receipts are hash-chained into a listing's trust record, so SLA claims are witnessed history, not vendor self-report, and a badge auto-degrades on witnessed downtime (SPEC §2): every probe appends a receipt {seq, ts, target_id, vantage, vantage_mode, scope, ok, status, latency_ms, prev_hash, hash} where hash = sha256(canonical_json(receipt_without_hash)) and prev_hash is the previous receipt's hash for that target (genesis = 64 zero hex chars). Availability and badge tier are recomputed only from receipts; no tool accepts a self-reported uptime/SLA input. Bench: the bench independently recomputed every sha256 from the SPEC canonical form — match; field/ts edits, single-receipt rehash, middle/first deletion, and reorder on store copies were all detected.

No self-report path + badge ladder (original bench P1/P4 PASS): 14/14 canonical self-report shapes (uptime, availability, sla, sla_claim, claimed_uptime, availability_claim, self_report, self_reported_uptime, full Checkly-dashboard payload) refused SELF_REPORT_NOT_ACCEPTED on every tool, creating no target and no receipts; 12 setter/import tool names all NO_SUCH_TOOL. Exactly the 5 spec tools exist, with no setter/import/edit or badge/self-report input in any schema. Badge derived only from receipts in the window: 0 → NO_WITNESSED_HISTORY; 1–4 @100% → INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY; 5 @100% → UP; 19/20 = 0.95 → UP; 9/10 = 0.90 → DEGRADED; 4/5 = 0.80 → DEGRADED; 7/10 = 0.70 → DOWN; window honored exactly (default 20, clamps at 100). Availability math exact: localhost sequence [200,503,200,404,200,503,201] → 4/7 = 0.5714285714285714; fixture error/down → 0.0; connection-refused localhost → ok=false status=0 receipt; 0 receipts → NO_WITNESSED_HISTORY, availability null; targets isolated.

Redirects never followed + crash-proof + structural refusal (v0.1.1 fixes for bench defects D1/D2/D3, re-bench PASS): probes use a no-redirect opener — the registered endpoint's own response (incl. 3xx, recorded with its true status) is the witnessed outcome, no same-origin/cross-origin/external hop is ever probed (re-bench 2a/2b/2c: same-origin 302→503, cross-origin 302→200, external-shaped 302, loop and chain all witness 302 only, destination hit counts unchanged 0→0). Malformed arguments can no longer kill the process: target_id type-checked in every tool, urlparse ValueError → clean validation error, dispatch + main-loop guards map unexpected exceptions to clean isError (re-bench P6: 21/21 checks, aggregating 82 fresh-process vectors, 0 crashes). Advertised schemas are enforced at dispatch (unknown keys rejected structurally) and self-report detection is normalized (case/camelCase/separators/suffixes + nested scan) — 19 variant shapes all refused, availability stayed exactly 0.5, receipt count and badge unchanged.

Honest scope — LOCAL ONLY: probes execute only against localhost (127.0.0.1/localhost/::1 HTTP) or fixture:// endpoints; 17 external/non-local URL shapes (incl. 127.0.0.1@evil.com, hex/decimal IP, sub.localhost, file:, ftp:) all SCOPE_EXTERNAL_REFUSED; conflicting re-register TARGET_CONFLICT, identical idempotent; LOCAL + local-simulated labels verified on receipts, trust record, badge, and verify outputs; fixture seed never auto-loaded. 'Vantage points' are distinct local probe identities (local-vantage-a/b/c), labeled vantage_mode: local-simulated in every artifact — they are NOT geographically independent and are never described as such. Python 3 standard library only; MCP over stdio; exactly 5 tools. No checkout/payment code exists — the $299/mo feed license is a pricing term only.

capabilities: Novel mechanism — runtimes poll a local policy endpoint; a BRAKE verdict halts the fleet within the poll interval, and the runtime returns a signed halt receipt proving it actually stopped (SPEC §2.1, the mechanism the bench verified verbatim via F-B14). Brake has no push channel, no remote kill, and no verb inside any runtime — a runtime that never polls cannot be halted by Brake, and Brake never claims otherwise.

HALTED only on proof — a fleet is HALTED only when every enrolled runtime has a valid, in-window, counter-signed halt receipt bound to the verdict's hash. Absence of a receipt is never evidence of a halt: the complementary terminal state is UNPROVEN-HALT, stated on the episode pack's face and never softened. Late receipts are recorded as defects and never amend a closed episode; a stale verdict closes its episode STALE-UNDELIVERED.

Offline-recomputable episode pack — the pack (fleet record, verdict token, poll records, receipts, defects, close statement, hash chain) recomputes via receipt_verify executing the full §6.4 procedure: fleet-record hash recomputed from the full record in the pack and bound to the signed chain, chain and poll-record signatures verified, receipts bound to recorded poll deliveries, post-halt attestations recomputed against the Brake-side fixture task log exported in the pack, and the close state derived mechanically from the enrolled roster — a partial fleet's pack cannot be re-hashed into HALTED (re-bench D1 forgery now fails at verifier step 1 with no key).

capabilities: Novel mechanism — vendor-run scorecards embed a spot-check hook in every check entry as it runs; a separate verifier harness draws a random sample from the SEALED scorecard and re-runs those checks, so a fabricated self-bench is statistically detectable. Commit-then-sample: the scorecard is sealed (hash-chained, vendor-signed) before any sample exists, and the verifier nonce is generated verifier-side (secret seed in keys/ + fresh per-draw CSPRNG), revealed only in the sample manifest after the seal is verified — the vendor cannot precompute or influence the sample (re-bench D1: 6,005 candidate nonces from public state matched none; supplied nonces refused VERIFIER_NONCE_REFUSED / VENDOR_NONCE_REFUSED).

Honest receipt arithmetic — the receipt states its power on its face: at sample size k and fabricated fraction f, detection probability is 1 − (1−f)^k (default k = 30, powered at f ≥ 0.10 → detection ≥ 95%). Verdicts: VERIFIED_SAMPLE · DIVERGENT (mismatched check ids named) · UNVERIFIABLE (non-deterministic or secret-requiring checks resolve here, never to a silent pass). A check without a hook is labelled HOOKLESS on the scorecard's face and sits outside every sample and every verified claim; unverifiable scorecards export only as DOWNGRADED_EXPORT.

Authenticated artefacts — the seal signature binds the head hash, all counts, and the format version (tampered counts/format → SEAL_INVALID); recompute verifies receipt signatures, the outcome record chain, and the rerun chain head, and rejects extra, missing, or forged outcomes (BENCHKIT_VERIFY_FAIL). Verifier verbs require the verifier token (VERIFIER_TOKEN_REQUIRED otherwise). Idempotent replay: resubmitting an issued (scorecard_hash, verifier_nonce) pair returns the recorded manifest + receipt with no new draw and no double metering.

Configuration fence (F-B14) — startup hard-exits code 2 with CONFIG_FENCE_REFUSED:<class> on a non-local endpoint, a live-key string, a vendor/verifier-nonce config, a non-test value_class, or an Assay-price / Cupel-checkout / buy-Assay-licence config; live-URL server descriptors are refused at run_begin with the same named codes. Disjoint surfaces: vendor = exactly 5 tools, verifier = exactly 5; cross-surface calls return the identical NO_SUCH_TOOL refusal as a nonsense name.

capabilities: Novel mechanism — a synthetic-counterparty mint whose every artifact carries a provable synthetic watermark (SPEC §4.4): overt markers (synthetic: true, value_class: "test", mint_id, watermark_id wm_…, and the mockmint_ ref namespace), a Herald-signed attestation (RS256 JWS) bound to artifact_hash ‖ mint_id ‖ watermark_id ‖ artifact_type, and a per-mint artifact hash chain in the ledger export — so watermarked test artifacts are detectable as synthetic wherever they surface, within the stated detection boundary below.

Out-of-band trust anchor only (SPEC §5.1) — verification never trusts keys supplied by the presenter: public keys come only from an explicit trusted_public_keys argument, the MOCKMINT_TRUSTED_KEYS_FILE config file, or the local key store's pinned public keys (keys/public-keys.json). Keys embedded in an artifact, mint record, or ledger export are ignored for trust — a fully self-consistent forged ecosystem fails VERIFY_FAIL, a removed anchor refuses rather than trusting presenter material, and genuine outsider verification (export + pinned public keys alone) passes 12/12 (re-bench F-K10). No private key material exists anywhere in the shipped tree outside the gitignored keys/ store (keys/ dir 700, keys.json 600); clean checkouts regenerate fixture keys locally by design.

Detection boundary, stated exactly as measured (SPEC §11.2 / F-K11 as amended by Amendment A1 — the listing must state the bare-payload limit, not oversell detection): mockmint_detect flags SYNTHETIC_MOCKMINT when (a) the full watermark verifies against the out-of-band pinned trust anchor, or (b) the watermark object is stripped but at least one identifying structural field survives — mint_id, artifact_id, or a mockmint_-namespace counterparty_ref — and that field resolves against the ledger export. An identifying field that does not resolve is UNVERIFIABLE. Records retaining only non-identifying fields (parent_ref, artifact_hash, overt flags) or bare payload values are NO_WATERMARK_FOUND — the honest limit (SPEC §14 Q-K1): values hand-copied as bare payload, with every structural field removed, carry nothing of the artifact, and no artifact-carried mechanism can detect that. Re-bench strip battery: 12/12 SYNTHETIC at every identifying-field level including single-field L5/L6/L7; 12/12 NO_WATERMARK_FOUND at the non-identifying and bare-payload levels; claim == measurement at every level.

Minting is deterministic under a seed; mint records are minter + Herald counter-signed in a hash-chained ledger. A real-name imitation linter refuses lookalike display names including spaced/leet variants, and a payload linter refuses real-credential/identifier shapes. Malformed input to any tool returns a named refusal and the server process survives (re-bench: 58 hostile calls across all 9 tools, 0 raises). capabilities: Novel mechanism — every review is bound to a sealed purchase receipt, and the corpus ships with a recomputable verified-share statistic: each submitted review is checked against a sealed purchase receipt (consumed as-is in the Till/Settleseal format) and, on a verified match of receipt + item + seller, bound to that receipt's hash inside a counter-signed, hash-chained review record (binding outcomes: BOUND_VERIFIED · UNBOUND_NO_RECEIPT · UNBOUND_RECEIPT_UNVERIFIABLE · UNBOUND_ITEM_MISMATCH · UNBOUND_SELLER_MISMATCH). Reviews without a verifiable binding are sealed too, labelled UNBOUND — the corpus is complete, not curated — and a replayed receipt is quarantined (RECEIPT_REPLAY) and never enters the corpus.

Recomputable verified-share statistic — at snapshot time the server computes the verified share over the sealed corpus (exact unreduced rational, e.g. 7/10, never a bare percentage) and counter-signs it into a snapshot record stating numerator, denominator, unbound counts by reason, and tombstoned/superseded exclusions on its face. The exported corpus pack contains the full record stream, binding-check transcripts, and labelled fixture verification keys, so any third party recomputes the statistic and the corpus head hash from the pack alone (re-bench F-R12 decisive: fresh process, pack alone, Fraction(7,10) exact). A corpus that fails recompute exports only as DOWNGRADED_EXPORT with statistic_status UNVERIFIED — never upgraded post-hoc; verified_share_get withholds the statistic on a downgraded corpus (UNVERIFIED + downgrade reason).

Fail-closed discipline — startup refuses with CONFIG_FENCE_REFUSED:<class> (exit 2, no state written) on any live marketplace/API endpoint, live key, production-corpus or real-review import path, value_class other than test, or receipt-format patch config, on both the env and config-file routes (re-bench: 15 hostile env configs + 5 config-file classes, all refused). Malformed input to any of the 11 tools returns a named refusal with zero corpus mutation and the process survives. Disjoint surfaces: marketplace = exactly 6 tools, auditor = exactly 5 (auditor verbs require the auditor token, fail-closed when unconfigured); no verb issues a receipt, edits or deletes a sealed record, or reclassifies an UNBOUND record post-seal. Corrections are superseding records and removals are tombstone records — the chain keeps both and exclusions are counted on the snapshot's face.

Honest scope — LOCAL / simulator, fixture corpus ONLY: v0.1.1 is exercised only against a fixture marketplace corpus (fixture listings, fixture reviews, fixture purchase receipts). No live marketplace, no real review, no real buyer is touched. Reviewseal attests binding and corpus integrity only: an UNBOUND review is unbound — a fact about evidence, never a verdict that the review is fake, fraudulent, or inauthentic — and the unbound share is never rendered as a fake rate. It does not verify a review's truth, quality, or authorship and computes no star averages as claims. Reviewer identity appears only as a pseudonymous hash ref; no receipt payload beyond the binding fields enters any record or export.

capabilities: Novel mechanism — agent identity-continuity chains across model/config changes: every change in an agent's life appends a signed link to a single hash-chained identity chain rooted at a genesis link, so a counterparty verifies offline, recomputably, that the agent in front of them descends link by link from the principal they originally trusted — 'same principal, new model' instead of re-trusting from zero. Continuity proves continuity, not trustworthiness: a verifying chain asserts same-principal lineage only, nothing about the new model's capability, safety, or fitness.

Fork freeze + principal-only resolution — key rotation and model change are distinct link types, never conflated (a combined change is two links, rotation first). Two valid children of one head freeze the chain FORKED; only a signed resolution link naming the surviving and repudiated branch heads resumes it, and the repudiated branch stays in exports, labelled. Revocation is terminal: the full chain verifies REVOKED, a prefix verifies CONTINUOUS_AS_OF:<seq> labelled historical, never current standing. A missing link is BROKEN:missing-link:<seq> — there is no partial-continuity verdict — and unwitnessed link sets receive no receipt at all, only a DOWNGRADED_CHAIN_EXPORT.

Consume-or-refuse caller pins (v0.1.2, condition C1) — continuity_verify / continuity_verify_prefix take the presented chain plus public keys: a caller pinning a principal to a key ref, or an expected head hash, is honored (a chain anchored under a different key does not verify against that caller's anchor). Every part of a supplied public_keys argument must resolve to a pin (supported shapes enumerated in README: key-ref lists; principal -> key ref / ref list / secret / descriptor; key ref -> secret or descriptor; sole keys/key_refs/public_keys wrappers) or the call refuses PIN_SHAPE_UNRECOGNISED with no verdict and no receipt — pin material is never silently ignored (spot re-bench: 28/28 named-shape + 102/102 variant probes refuse; every supported shape provably binds).

Honest scope — LOCAL / fixture ONLY: v0.1.2 builds and verifies chains over fixture identity events with fixture principals/models/keys (HMAC fixture keys via a fixture Herald interface stub; signing material lives only in the local gitignored keys/ store, mode 600, never in source). No live registry, no network fetch, no production identity store, no live identity claim. Startup fails closed with CONFIG_FENCE_REFUSED:<class> on any live-registry URL, non-fixture Herald endpoint, non-test value class, or key material outside keys/. Verification never writes the chain store (metering is an in-memory record only).

capabilities: Novel mechanism — regulator publications are witnessed on release and machine-mapped to the subscriber's own control/product set, so 'this rule changed' arrives as 'these three of your controls are affected.' A publication enters only as a witnessed record (content hash + footprint + release stamp, witness counter-signed); the subscriber's control set enters only as a sealed, versioned declaration (subscriber-signed, witness counter-signed); the mapping is a deterministic boolean anchor match (citation ∈ declared anchors OR topic-key intersection) under the versioned rule set regulens-rules/1.0 — no model inference, no embeddings, no per-run judgement. The output is a signed impact receipt naming affected declared controls with the triggering anchor + passage refs, recomputable offline from the receipt + witnessed publication + sealed set + rule-set version alone (spot re-bench F-R13: P4 × S-B recomputed exactly, affected B1, B2, B3).

Single trust anchor + downgrade law (v0.1.2, conditions N1–N3) — verification pins to the local keys/ store only: production code contains zero reads of fixtures/fixture-keys.json (that file is public keys only, informational, never consulted); rotating or deleting both keys/ files makes pre-rotation artifacts fail IMPACT_VERIFY_FAIL:1, never RECOMPUTED, and a missing store raises the named KEY_STORE_MISSING:<role> class — issuance over missing keys refuses SIGNATURE_INVALID with no sealed output. A receipt that fails recompute at any step exports only as DOWNGRADED_IMPACT_EXPORT (verified: false, failing step on its face) — no tool path upgrades, repairs, or edits a receipt, a witnessed publication, or a sealed set in place; a republication or redeclaration produces a new record under its own triple.

§6.2 face posture on every envelope — the verbatim standing face text rides the top level of every emitted envelope class (14/14 probed in the spot re-bench, including server ToolError / generic-error envelopes and the downgraded export): 'Impact receipt — a deterministic mapping over your declared control set only. Not legal advice; not a compliance determination. Controls you did not declare were not mapped (see set_hash).' Regulens output is an impact receipt, never legal advice; not a compliance determination. It never states a remediation instruction, required action, or deadline, and it maps only controls the subscriber declared — controls not declared were not mapped, and a nil receipt (affected: []) is a first-class recomputable artifact proving only that the mapping over the declared set found no anchor match.

Honest scope — LOCAL / simulator, fixture corpus ONLY: v0.1.2 runs over fixture regulator publications (P1–P4, invented fixture citations) and fixture subscriber control sets (S-A: 5 controls, S-B: 3 controls), local stdio only, all artifacts value_class: test. NO live ingestion exists or is claimed: no live regulator site is fetched, scraped, polled, or republished, there is no dormant live-ingestion path to flip, and startup refuses CONFIG_FENCE_REFUSED:<class> on any live-source / HTTP-client / non-test configuration. Live ingestion is gated on the SPEC §10 source-terms review (the source-terms gate is unbuilt by design) plus counsel review of the §11.2 'not legal advice' language — a post-gate, re-benched code change, not a configuration flip.

capabilities: Novel mechanism — causal attribution as a RECOMPUTE over hash-chained multi-agent records (SPEC §2.1): Scapegoat verifies every chain in the presented set, recomputes each action's conformance against the governing mandate/policy it cites, and names the causal action — the earliest record whose deviation first made the failure inevitable on the recorded path — in a Herald-signed verdict (methodology scapegoat-attribution/1.0) that ships the proof path: governing authority → causal action → failure record, each entry with its hash and recomputed conformance checks, so any third party re-runs §6.4 from the export alone and reaches the same verdict or names the step where the pack fails.

Presented proof path bound to the signed verdict (v0.1.2, condition C1 / defect N1 closed, Verity spot re-bench spot-scapegoat-012.md) — proof_verify step 2 recomputes the signed proof_path_head_hash over the PRESENTED path (a dropped, stripped, reordered, duplicated, or substituted entry fails at :2), step 4 requires the presented path to equal the recomputed walk — ids, order, roles, stream, seq — with every entry's conformance_checks matching the recomputation (a check-edited trail fails at :4), and re-pointing the head hash dies at step 1 on the Herald signature, because the head field sits inside the signed verdict core. Spot re-bench: 6/6 N1 table rows and 11/11 bench-devised path attacks FAIL at exactly the named steps; the honest pack PASSes.

Record-bounded honesty — where the records do not determine a unique causal action, the verdict is UNATTRIBUTED at full standing with the reason named (NO_DEVIATION / MULTIPLE_FIRST_DEVIATIONS / CAUSAL_GAP / SET_DEFECT / NO_GOVERNING_AUTHORITY), never a plausible party picked to fill the gap. The verdict path contains no model call, no free-text reasoning, and no operator override; no tool accepts a party's narrative (NARRATIVE_FIELD_REJECTED); Scapegoat creates no records, repairs no chain, and fills no gap — defects (HASH_MISMATCH, SIGNATURE_INVALID, SEQ_GAP, …) are stated on the verdict's face, and a record that failed integrity never carries an attribution through the causal window (tampered causal window degrades to UNATTRIBUTED: CAUSAL_GAP; tampered downstream record is stated as a defect on an ATTRIBUTED verdict).

Honest scope — LOCAL, fixture record sets ONLY: v0.1.2 recomputes over fixture hash-chained record sets with fixture RS256 keys held only in the local gitignored keys/ store (private keys mode 600, never committed; proof_verify pins public keys from keys/public-keys.json only — a key carried in a pack is checked against the pin, never trusted). No real dispute, no real record set, and no real party is adjudicated. A verdict is causal evidence from a recompute — NOT a legal liability determination, not a legal fault finding, and never stated to bind any party; evidentiary use in real disputes is a counsel-gated later phase (SPEC §10), not built. Closed surface: exactly 5 tools; no record-creation, chain-repair, re-run, override, party-naming, or remedy verb exists.

capabilities: Novel mechanism — per-class Herald-counter-signed acceptance receipts (SPEC §2.1): a sponsor signs a separate acceptance receipt for each action class they sponsor (payments / publishing / contracting), each with its own scope terms, limits, and validity window, instead of one blanket terms acceptance at onboarding. Signing payments signs nothing else; the other classes remain UNACCEPTED until separately signed. There is no verb, field, or default that accepts all classes or an unnamed class.

Scoped like a mandate — each presented action is checked in a fixed order (class/scope match → limits → validity/revocation) and the first failure names the refusal (CLASS_MISMATCH, SCOPE_MISMATCH, LIMIT_EXCEEDED, ACCEPTANCE_EXPIRED, ACCEPTANCE_REVOKED, ACCEPTANCE_SUPERSEDED, …). Aggregate limits are recomputed from prior check records in the chain, never stored.

Chained, revocable, time-bounded, offline-recomputable — receipts append to the sponsored party's hash-chained record stream; revocation and supersession are new chained records, prospective only. Any third party recomputes the whole pack offline from the exported pack plus pinned keys alone: enrolment hashes, sponsor + Herald signatures, terms-hash binding, chain hashes, per-class status derivation (an UNACCEPTED class is proven by derivation over the complete chain, not by absence from a summary), and every check record's outcome. Bench-decisive fixture F-S14: payments ACTIVE while publishing and contracting derive UNACCEPTED from the same pack, and the same action descriptor returns COVERED-BY-RECEIPT as payments and CLASS_MISMATCH as publishing/contracting.

The liability fence (SPEC §11.2, verbatim): A Sponsorline receipt evidences that a sponsor signed stated acceptance terms for a stated action class at a stated time. It does not itself create, transfer, or enforce legal liability. Enforceability is a counsel question (§10) and is not claimed.

Honest scope — LOCAL stdio, fixture sponsors and parties ONLY: every artifact carries value_class "test"; no real sponsor is solicited, signed, or recorded; no live signing ceremony, production agent, counterparty, or external registry is contacted. Signing is a fixture HMAC stand-in for the Herald pattern (no live Herald key held); fixture keys are pinned out-of-band in the local gitignored keys/ store (mode 600, never committed) — a key presented inside a record or pack is never trusted. Closed surface: exactly 9 tools across 3 disjoint surfaces (sponsor / operator / verifier); no verb accepts on a sponsor's behalf, accepts multiple classes, edits, extends, deletes, backdates, or marks accepted.

capabilities: Novel mechanism — a continuous fingerprint chain over a payee's bank/rail details; any silent change blocks payment and issues a drift receipt — the classic vendor-bank-fraud pattern becomes impossible to hide. (That sentence describes the fixture chain's tamper-evidence property, not a real-world fraud guarantee — SPEC §11.4 fence, attached per the spec's honest-label rules.)

Fingerprint chain — fingerprint = sha256(canonical(payee_detail_set)) over a fixed field set (payee_ref, beneficiary_name, bank_id, account_id as fixture tokens only, rail, unit); every witnessed state appends one signed, hash-chained record, so rewriting history breaks every later hash. A check recomputes the presented fingerprint against the chain head: match → CLEAR; mismatch → BLOCK_DRIFT plus a signed drift receipt naming the changed field classes only — never values — with the last agreeing sequence and prior fingerprint. Silence is drift: a missing field, an added field, or a re-ordered canonical form does not match; a legitimate change is absorbed only by an explicit re-enrollment citing the drift receipt, and the seam stays in the chain permanently.

Offline recompute with pinned fixture keys — chain_verify recomputes every fingerprint, record hash, changed-field-class list and verdict from the source detail sets in an exported pack, using only the local pinned fixture keys (never keys presented inside a pack; a pack carrying keys fails at keys_pinned). The pinned fixture keys are HMAC secrets — they are NOT public keys, and no public or third-party verifiability is claimed at v0.1.1. An export is labelled witnessed:true / WITNESSED_EXPORT only when its embedded verifier transcript actually verified.

Completeness limits (bench condition C-4, on the face) — chain_verify proves the integrity of the records presented, NOT the completeness of the payee's history: a pack truncated to a prefix of the chain (receipts pruned consistently) verifies true as that shorter chain, because the pack format carries no external head-hash or length anchor; callers needing completeness must pin the head fingerprint and record count out-of-band (both are on the verify result's face). Appending an exact duplicate of a valid drift receipt still verifies (linkage is set-compared; the duplicate inflates the reported drift_receipts count, and no false history is created). The pack's own witnessed/export label is never trusted — the result label is re-derived from the recompute.

Export packs are NOT value-free (bench condition C-3, on the face) — chain_export packs contain the full fixture detail sets (enrollment, re-enrollment and check sets) by design, because drift classes and fingerprints are recomputed from them; the values are synthetic fixture tokens only (bank_fixture_…, acct_fixture_…), never real bank data, and packs must be handled as 'fixture tokens only' until a live-scope redesign. Honest scope — LOCAL stdio, fixture payee records ONLY: no live bank, rail, vendor-master, or payment system is touched and no real bank-account number enters any fixture. Morphguard never pays, settles, releases, or holds funds — a drift result is a verdict returned to the caller (CLEAR / BLOCK_DRIFT / BLOCK_UNKNOWN_PAYEE / BLOCK_CHAIN_DEFECT); payment execution, if the caller proceeds on a CLEAR, stays entirely with Till behind Till's existing gates. A CLEAR means only 'presented fixture details match the chain head' — nothing more. Closed surface: exactly 9 tools across 2 disjoint surfaces (caller 6 / operator 3); no pay/settle/release/hold/edit/delete verb exists on either surface. Startup is fail-closed: a real ABA-shaped routing token, a live-key string, a non-local endpoint, or value_class other than 'test' refuses startup.

capabilities: Novel mechanism (SPEC §2.1, verbatim) — an agent's full tool/permission configuration is sealed and streamed; every change emits a delta receipt to subscribers (employers, insurers, auditors). Mandatory gloss (SPEC §11.3): sealed = an operator declared this configuration, in this order, at these times — recompute it yourself.

Genesis seal + hash-chained delta stream — the full configuration is canonicalised, hashed, and sealed at config_seq 0, signed by the operator and counter-signed by Kitseal; every change is a delta record citing the exact head config_hash it applies to and the resulting config_hash, chained on dual spines (prev_hash record spine + base→result config spine). A delta citing anything but the current head is refused (DELTA_BASE_MISMATCH); the chain is append-only and fork-refusing, retirement is itself a delta, and sealed records are never edited or deleted. Every delta receipt carries the attestation verbatim: 'operator-declared configuration change; Kitseal attests presentation, sequence, and hashes — not runtime state.'

Offline recompute (SPEC §6.4) — a subscriber holding only the exported pack + pinned fixture keys recomputes the current configuration in a fresh process without asking Kitseal anything: config hashes, record hashes, both spines, the op digest, and both signatures (operator + Kitseal counter-signature) are recomputed against keys pinned out-of-band, never keys presented inside a record. A withheld receipt is detectable by sequence gap: the recompute stops at KITSEAL_VERIFY_FAIL:gap@<seq>, asserts no current configuration, and the export is labelled STALE_OR_PARTIAL. Verify-before-serve (v0.1.1, delta-bench C1/C2 closures): loadout_status, feed_read, and the pack face run the full chain verification over the records they serve before asserting any head hash, state, receipt, or chain_complete_through, and receipt_verify walks the presented chain from genesis to the receipt's record — an isolated record without chain context does not verify.

Honest scope — LOCAL stdio, fixture loadouts ONLY: configurations are operator-supplied fixture data, no real agent is sealed or streamed, Kitseal connects to no runtime, captures no configuration from any system, grants/revokes no permission, and is not a config-management tool, runtime monitor, or policy engine. Closed surface of exactly 9 dispatch entries (5 operator + 4 subscriber, disjoint; loadout_pack_export appears on both surfaces); no verb edits or deletes a sealed record, re-bases a delta onto a non-head hash, asserts a current configuration without recompute, captures a config from a runtime, or suppresses a delta from a subscriber feed. Startup is fail-closed (CONFIG_FENCE_REFUSED:<class>) on a live-key string, a non-local endpoint, a config source other than operator presentation, a runtime credential, or value_class other than 'test'. Signing is an HMAC-SHA256 fixture stand-in for the Herald pattern (bench observation F4); symmetric fixture keys mean the operator/Kitseal key holder set is a local trust domain, consistent with (local) scope.

capabilities: Novel mechanism (SPEC §2.1, with the §11.2 substitution applied) — the price + terms an agent saw are sealed at view time, so view-to-checkout drift is recomputable from the buyer-held pack by the buyer. Seal at view time + term-by-term diff — seal_hash = sha256(canonical(view_terms_object)) over the full §4.1 view terms object (price, fees, shipping, taxes as stated, quantity/availability terms, returns terms, subscription terms, and the listing version itself), each field also hashed individually (term_hashes) so drift is located, not just detected; there is no price-only mode — a checkout matching the headline price but drifting any other sealed term is DRIFT. Verification recomputes each sealed term's per-term hash from the presented checkout and returns MATCH, or on any mismatch a signed drift receipt naming each drifted term with its sealed vs presented per-term hashes (hashes only, except unit_price/total_all_in/shipping_as_stated amounts when those terms drift, SPEC §6.3). Verdicts: MATCH · DRIFT · LISTING_SUPERSEDED · EXPIRED_VIEW · SEAL_NOT_FOUND. A listing view never presented at view time can never be sealed retrospectively — a reconstructed view receives only an unsigned UNSEALED_SUMMARY, which the verifier rejects; downgrade law: unverifiable packs downgrade whole to UNWITNESSED_EXPORT, never upgraded.

Offline verification (SPEC §6.4) — a pure function of the buyer-held pack + pinned fixture keys alone: seal_hash and every term_hash recomputed from the pack's view terms, Herald signature and buyer counter-signature verified against keys pinned out-of-band (never keys carried inside the pack; counter-signature presence/absence must match the seal's face label), record chain walked gapless, drifted_terms + verdict re-derived per verification record including the expiry and superseded-version conditions, value_class 'test' required throughout; any step failing downgrades the whole pack with no partial verdict. Stored paths enforce the same discipline (v0.1.1, delta-bench C1–C3 closures): checkout_verify (fresh + idempotent), view_seal's idempotent return, seal_status, and drift_receipt_get recompute stored seal hashes/term hashes and verify record hashes, Herald signatures, counter-signatures, and receipt hashes before issuing any verdict or serving any stored record — any mismatch is a SEAL_DEFECT refusal, no verdict issued, no record appended, nothing tampered served.

capabilities: Novel mechanism (SPEC §2.1, verbatim) — a skill claim is a pointer to a bench-verdict receipt; a claim with no receipt renders as UNVERIFIED in a standard format counterparties and routers can filter on. The claim is a pointer, not a proof by assertion: a claim carries no grade, score, or verdict of its own (a claim carrying one is malformed and refused), and every verdict string in a rendering is copied mechanically from the receipt's face at verification time.

Verification recomputes everything from the presented artifacts + pinned keys alone — claim hash + publisher fixture signature; receipt hash recomputed and required to equal the claim's pointer; receipt bench signature verified against the bench key pinned out-of-band by receipt format (never a key taken from, or selected by, the record); subject, skill ref, scope (token-set containment over the pinned fixture vocabulary), pass-class verdict (pinned: PASS only), expiry, and revocation re-derived from the receipt's face; render hash recomputed and the Herald counter-signature verified. Two fixture receipt formats are consumed (benchkit-scorecard and assay-service-receipt) with identical rendered shape. Any parseable-but-failing receipt renders UNVERIFIED with a machine-readable reason (NO_RECEIPT, RECEIPT_HASH_MISMATCH, RECEIPT_SIGNATURE_INVALID, RECEIPT_SUBJECT_MISMATCH, RECEIPT_SKILL_MISMATCH, RECEIPT_SCOPE_NARROWER, RECEIPT_NON_PASS, RECEIPT_EXPIRED, RECEIPT_REVOKED, WITHDRAWN); unparseable artifacts and malformed claims refuse. Downgrade law: any export that cannot be recompute-verified is labelled UNVERIFIED_EXPORT on its face, with no path back to a VERIFIED rendering over the same export. capabilities: Novel mechanism (SPEC §2.1, verbatim) — similarity scoring over registered agent identities (name, purpose, capability profile) issues a collision verdict before an agent launches under a confusing identity. Scoring version namesake-score/1.0 is pinned and purely mechanical — no model call, no randomness, no discretionary adjustment — so every component score recomputes offline from the candidate, the snapshot, and the pinned scoring version alone.

Scoring + verification recompute everything — per registered identity: name similarity (normalised edit similarity + token-set Jaccard over case/diacritic/punctuation-folded names; exact normalised match = 1.0), purpose similarity (token Jaccard over declared-purpose token sets), capability similarity (Jaccard over capability-profile ref sets); composite = 0.5·name + 0.3·purpose + 0.2·capability (rounded 6dp); verdict over the maximum composite (REVIEW ≥ 0.40, COLLISION ≥ 0.70, exact-normalised-name match forces COLLISION regardless of composite), with the top-3 identities, full component breakdowns, thresholds, and snapshot id + hash on the verdict's face. namesake_verify recomputes candidate/snapshot hashes, re-derives the normalised name + purpose tokens, recomputes every component score + composite + top-k, re-derives the verdict (incl. the exact-name override), recomputes the §4.5 chain head (candidate → snapshot pin → score records → verdict), and verifies the builder submission signature + Herald signature against pinned out-of-band keys only (a key supplied inside a record fails). capabilities: Novel mechanism (SPEC §2.1, verbatim) — each answer ships with its primary-source pointer plus a retrieval receipt (fetcher, time, content hash) — provenance at the granularity of one fact. A bibliography or link list without a per-fact retrieval receipt is not this product (SPEC §0.6).

Per-fact retrieval receipts, hash-chained and sealed — for each fixture answer fact, the named fixture fetcher (fixture-fetcher/1.0) retrieves exactly the pointed-to bytes from a fixture source store; each receipt seals source_pointer (store_ref, locator, byte_range | record_ref) + fetcher identity/version + retrieved_at (RFC 3339 UTC, validated at seal and on verify) + content_hash + byte_length; receipts chain per answer (record_hash = sha256(canonical(record minus hash/seal fields) || prev_hash), seq 1-based gapless), and the receipt-stream head is sealed with the pinned fixture HMAC Herald stand-in (herald-fixture). No skipping: a sealed answer has a receipt for every fact — FACT_WITHOUT_RECEIPT, POINTER_UNRESOLVABLE:<fact_id> (draft UNSEALABLE), RECEIPT_DUPLICATE, and FETCHER_UNNAMED are named refusals that mutate nothing; sealing is idempotent on (answer_hash, receipt_set_hash) with exactly 1 metering point per sealed answer.

Offline verification + re-fetch verdicts, reported separately — sourceseal_receipt_verify recomputes answer_hash, every record_hash, the chain, receipt_set_hash, and the pinned seal from a presented bundle alone (no re-fetch); sourceseal_source_reverify re-fetches each pointer and returns per-fact verdicts only (SOURCE_UNCHANGED / SOURCE_CHANGED with both hashes / SOURCE_GONE), never a rolled-up verdict. Downgrade law (SPEC §6.4): an answer whose receipts do not verify exports only as UNSEALED_EXPORT (sealed:false); a later source change does NOT downgrade the original receipt — a valid receipt over a since-changed source is both receipt: valid and SOURCE_CHANGED, never conflated.

Stored-serve hardening (bench conditions C1–C6, all CLOSED at v0.1.3) — sourceseal_receipt_get and the idempotent re-serve path of sourceseal_answer_seal verify before serving (full receipt_verify recompute), bind the stored bundle to the requested answer (answer_id / answer_hash / receipt_set_hash against entry, key, and recomputation), survive malformed store shapes with structured downgrades/refusals (no uncaught exception escapes), serve only canonical constructed faces (code-constant face fields, computed sealed/verified booleans, exact key sets at bundle/answer/fact/pointer/receipt level; injected extra keys, face tampers, and receipt seal/signature keys are stripped or defect, never echoed verified), and validate the whole store (keys, entries, metering bijection) before any write — a garbage sibling, renamed key, or inconsistent metering refuses a fresh seal with MALFORMED_STORE and zero writes.

Decisive fixture F-S9 — bench-reproduced at v0.1.0 and as a regression at every delta re-bench through v0.1.3: in fresh processes, from the shipped bundle + pinned keys alone, receipt_verify confirms every receipt and source_reverify recomputes every content_hash from the fixture stores (all SOURCE_UNCHANGED; bencher also recomputed hashes independently from raw store files); one source mutated after seal → receipt chain still valid, reverify returns SOURCE_CHANGED for exactly that fact. A pointer-only (hash-blind) verifier cannot pass this test.

capabilities: Novel mechanism (SPEC §2.1, verbatim) — creep is detected against the sealed price history from the original authorization, so a merchant's gradual increases are measured against proof, not memory.

Sealed baseline or nothing (SPEC L5) — at authorization time the original price terms (baseline amount, unit, period, the authorization's own per-charge + cumulative thresholds, any scheduled steps) are hash-sealed and Herald-signed (RS256 JWS, per-term hashes); a charge stream with no original authorization sealed at authorization time can receive no measurement — retrospective baselines are refused, only an unsigned UNSEALED_SUMMARY (sealed:false) can be issued for a reconstructed stream, and the verifier rejects it as a Faircharge artifact

Pinned creep rule (SPEC §2.2, integer minor units / basis points only, no floats, unmappable units refused never coerced) — per-charge delta vs the amount expected given the stream so far (scheduled-step amount effective at that index, else previous charge in the current seam segment, else the segment baseline) and cumulative drift always vs the current seam segment's baseline; verdicts WITHIN_TERMS / CREEP_PER_CHARGE / CREEP_CUMULATIVE / CREEP_BOTH, stream roll-up = worst per-charge verdict; a stream can verdict CREEP_CUMULATIVE while every individual charge is within its per-charge delta — that asymmetry is the mechanism; an unpinned dimension is not judged and every receipt states dimension_unpinned for it (§6.3)

Signed creep receipts + measurement pack — on any non-WITHIN_TERMS measurement a Herald-signed creep receipt names the charge, the sealed baseline values, expected + presented amounts, delta, cumulative drift, the sealed threshold(s) crossed, and the measurement record id; measurement_pack_export assembles terms + seal + all measurement records + all presented charge objects + creep receipts + re-authorization records + a signed head anchor (record_hash + record_count) as the deliverable to Docket — Faircharge supplies the recomputable measurement, Docket/counsel decide what, if anything, it breaches

Offline verification (SPEC §6.4) — measurement_verify recomputes per-term hashes, the whole hash chain, Herald signatures (+ caller counter-signature presence matching its on-face label), every expected_amount / delta / cumulative_drift / verdict, the roll-up, and every receipt from the pack + pinned public keys alone (keys/pinned-public.json only; key material in tool args or inside a pack is refused pre-verification); decisive fixture F-FC8 passes in a fresh process with an empty data dir; any step failing returns FAIRCHARGE_VERIFY_FAIL:<step>, no partial verdict, and the pack downgrades whole to UNWITNESSED_EXPORT — unverifiable ⇒ downgraded, never upgraded

Re-authorization seam (SPEC §3.2) — a genuinely re-authorized price enters only as an explicit re-authorization record citing the prior seal; the old baseline and all pre-seam measurements stay in history permanently and post-seam charges measure against the new baseline; no charge, verdict, or caller assertion can create a seam implicitly; state + current baseline are derived from the signed chain at read (post-close measurements are refused; the verifier refuses measurements after a stream_close)

capabilities: Novel mechanism (SPEC §2.1, verbatim) — burn-trajectory forecasting over sealed budget mandates intervenes before breach — throttle, escalate, or abort — and the intervention itself is receipted.

Forecast over the sealed record (SPEC §2.2.1) — after each spend record is appended, Burnline recomputes cumulative burn and the projected breach point from the sealed record set alone under the pinned model burnline-linear/1.0 (exact rational arithmetic, ceiling rounding, no floats in signed objects); every forecast cites the record-chain head it was computed over — a forecast over an unstated record set does not exist

Intervention before breach (SPEC §2.2.2) — when the projection crosses a mandate-carried threshold (warn / escalate / abort fractions, strictly increasing in (0,1], never defaulted), the corresponding verdict issues while the recomputed burn is still below the cap, in threshold order only; a single record crossing two thresholds issues the highest verdict only, with the skipped thresholds named; an intervention first issued at or after breach is a LATE_INTERVENTION defect, not an intervention

The intervention itself is receipted (SPEC §2.2.3) — every verdict is a signed intervention receipt hash-chained into the forecast stream, binding mandate hash ↔ record-chain head at forecast time ↔ projected breach point ↔ verdict, so a third party can recompute offline that the verdict was the one the pinned model produces over those records, issued at that head

Offline verification (SPEC §6.4) — forecast_verify recomputes the mandate hash, spend chain, every forecast, and every receipt's first-crossing + pre-breach position from the exported pack + pinned public keys alone, in a fresh process with no Burnline state; decisive fixture F-BU14 passes byte-identically on rerun (bench-reproduced: ABORT burn 3100 < cap 10000); any step failing returns BURNLINE_VERIFY_FAIL:<step> with no partial verdict, and an unrecomputable pack is labelled downgraded: true on its face, never upgraded post-hoc; unsealed inputs yield only UNSEALED_EXPORT, which the verifier rejects as a Burnline artifact

Verify-before-anything hardening (bench conditions C1–C7 + O2 + O3, all CLOSED at v0.1.5) — stored reads, the stream_open idempotent echo, spend_append and stream_close all run full stored-stream verification (chain, burn, state, signatures, ack/defect/receipt recomputation, exact per-type and store-container key sets) before serving, minting, or transitioning; fabricated or suppressed acks/defects and flipped receipt content fields fail with named steps, foreign store keys are refused and never re-persisted, and no signed close or receipt is ever minted over unverified bytes

Honest failure semantics (SPEC §3.4, on the face of the pack) — a runtime that ignores a verdict is chained as VERDICT_UNACKNOWLEDGED and the stream continues (Burnline never re-issues or claims the spend stopped); a cap jump with no prior threshold crossing closes BREACHED with the NO_PRIOR_INTERVENTION_POSSIBLE defect — no intervention receipt is issued or backdated

Verdict-not-enforcement fence (SPEC §0.4 / §11, on the face of the listing) — Burnline issues verdicts only: it holds no spend authority, blocks no transaction itself, and moves no money; nothing certifies live budget enforcement, real Herald/Meter/Till interop, or that a verdict stops spend

Surfacing proofs + offline verification (SPEC §4.5 / §6.4) — a proof binds receipt hash ↔ render hash ↔ disclosure-render hash ↔ buying-agent ref; receipt_verify recomputes placement hashes, both receipt signatures, the hash chain, mechanical status derivation, and every proof from the exported pack + pinned fixture keys alone, in a fresh process; any failure returns SHELFSPACE_VERIFY_FAIL:<step> with no partial verdict, and imported sponsorship claims receive at most UNVERIFIED_IMPORT.

capabilities: A PASS verdict is scan evidence, not a guarantee of safety or non-defamation.
Classes scanned by this release: PII and secrets. Classes outside those two are not scanned, and a PASS is not evidence about them.
This release does not scan for defamation-risk: defamation-risk detection is excluded from the certified scope of this version, and a PASS verdict is not evidence about defamation.

Secrets detection (on seeded fixtures): private-key headers, AWS, GitHub and prefixed tokens, bearer and JWT tokens, keyword assignments including JSON and compound key names, Authorization headers in any scheme, URL userinfo passwords, standalone 32-char hex tokens, and high-entropy tokens — 100% recall and 100% precision on seeded fixtures (fresh bench corpus, rates computed from signed receipts).

PII detection (on seeded fixtures): email addresses; Social Security numbers in dashed, dotted, spaced, and contiguous forms (SSA-validity gated); payment cards in grouped and contiguous forms (Luhn-gated); and phone numbers in domestic formats and E.164 international formats — 100% recall and 100% precision on seeded fixtures (spec thresholds ≥95% recall / ≥90% precision).

Phone scope: international phone detection covers E.164 (`+`-prefixed) forms, grouped or contiguous. A foreign number dialled with a `00` prefix, or written in national format without a leading `+`, is not detected as an international number; however, if its trailing digits happen to form a US/Canada (NANP) number pattern, the domestic phone detector will flag that trailing pattern. National-format foreign numbers whose digits do not form a NANP pattern are not detected.

Hex scope: standalone hex detection is capped at 32 chars — a standalone 32-char hex token is flagged; a hex string of 40 or more chars is detected only with assignment or header context, and standalone 40+ hex is not flagged.

Every verdict is a Herald-signed receipt bound to the content hash: any one-byte change to the content fails offline verification at step 1, and a receipt signed under any keys other than the pinned Herald/scanner keys fails at step 2. Detected secrets and PII appear in receipts, exports, and persisted artifacts by span and hash only — never as raw values. Unverifiable artifacts export only as UNVERIFIED_EXPORT.

capabilities: Novel mechanism (SPEC §2.1, verbatim) — every eval score carries an expiry computed from measured model/tool drift rates; consumers get a 'stale eval' verdict when a score outlives its evidence.

Pinned estimator sandclock/1.0 — least-squares slope of drift magnitude over time over all presented observations for the subject, computed in exact rational arithmetic, floored at 0; DRIFT_BUDGET = 1/10, MIN_DRIFT_OBS = 3, MIN_SPAN_DAYS = 7, MIN_EXPIRY_DAYS = 1, MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS = 180; expiry = issued_at + DRIFT_BUDGET / drift_rate, clamped to the pinned bounds with the clamp recorded on the record's face; below the evidence minimums the outcome is INSUFFICIENT_DRIFT_EVIDENCE — no expiry is issued and no default TTL exists anywhere in the product.

Decisive fixture F-S13 stands from the bench record — two fixture scorecards issued the same fixture day, fast drifter vs near-frozen subject, same pinned budget: expiries 10 days vs the 180-day clamp in the drift-implied order, split verdicts at day 30 (STALE_EVAL / CURRENT), reproduced exactly by fresh-process recompute from scorecards + evidence sets + public keys alone; a fixed-TTL implementation fails by construction.

Evidence-decay fence (SPEC §11.2, verbatim discipline) — expiry is evidence-decay arithmetic, not a claim the score was wrong. Every expiry, check record, and receipt states on its face: the estimator version (sandclock/1.0), the drift budget and clamp bounds in force, the evidence count and span, and the computed expires_at, in the permitted sense only: "this score's evidence decays past budget 1/10 at measured drift rate <r> under estimator sandclock/1.0; the score is stale as evidence after <expires_at>." Sandclock measures no current performance, never re-runs an eval, never edits a score, and never blocks a consumer from using a stale score — it issues the verdict; consumers decide.

Residual limit (SPEC §11.2, on every bundle and export, verbatim in substance): This bundle proves what the capturing fetcher was served, at the witness time, under the certificate presented to it. Eclipse Assay and Eclipse Cupel are internal tools, not products: this product has no dependency on them, no integration with them, and no buy path, price, licence, or checkout for them anywhere.

problem_statements: Web evidence today is a screenshot, a saved HTML file, or a log line — each separable, alterable, and silent on who served it: a page capture without its certificate cannot prove which server (or which impersonator) supplied the content

I need content, serving context, and server identity bound indivisibly at capture time — one hash-chained, signed bundle artifact — so recombining parts from different captures after the fact breaks verification by name

I need the bundle's limit printed on its face: it proves what the capturing fetcher was served at the witness time under the presented certificate — never what anyone else was served, and never admissibility, notarization equivalence, or that the content was true
products.tagline: Web-evidence capture witness over fixture captures — page captures seal content, headers, and the TLS certificate together as one hash-chained, Herald-signed bundle proving what was served, by whom, and when. PASS-CONDITIONAL (local, fixture captures) — local stdio, fixture captures only, value_class "test"; no live web capture exists in v0.1. This bundle proves what the capturing fetcher was served, at the witness time, under the certificate presented to it. A server may serve different content to other fetchers, at other times, or under other certificates — the bundle says nothing about what anyone else was served.
